algorithm.title: Evaluation of Knee Pain Without Recent Injury

cell.label: Knee pain, no recent injury. Hot, swollen joint or fever?
Aspirate joint: cell count, Gram stain, culture, crystals
cell.path: Bacteria or very high white count

cell.label: Red flags: night or unremitting pain, weight loss, history of cancer?
Age 45 or older, pain with activity, morning stiffness 30 minutes or less, joint line pain?
Where is the pain?
cell.path: Anterior pain with stairs, squatting, or sitting
Below the kneecap, worse with jumping

cell.label: Septic arthritis. Urgent orthopedic referral and antibiotics.
Gout or calcium pyrophosphate (CPPD) arthritis. Treat the flare.
Rheumatology referral (rheumatoid, reactive, or Lyme arthritis).
Probable knee osteoarthritis. Clinical diagnosis; X-ray optional. Exercise, weight loss, topical then oral NSAIDs. Arthroscopy not recommended.
Patellofemoral pain. Hip and knee strengthening.
Iliotibial band syndrome. Activity change, stretching, strengthening.
Pes anserine bursitis. Exercise, ice, NSAIDs.
X-ray; consider orthopedic or sports medicine referral. MRI only if it would change management.

footnotes.footnote: Hip disease can present as knee pain, especially SCFE in adolescents.
